title: Broad drinking-water coverage coexists with uneven household responsibility and unresolved replacement risk
source_unit: EPA drinking-water infrastructure assessments and CDC Environmental Health Tracking drinking-water indicators
geography: United States; national public-water and private-well coverage, service-line projections, and infrastructure needs

observations.period: 2025-2026; drinking-water infrastructure and lead service-line need

denominator.unit: U.S. drinking-water systems and projected service-line counts; source-specific universes

unknown_lines_predicted_lead.unit: service lines predicted to be lead from unknown-material reporting

twenty_year_drinking_water_need.unit: billion dollars of assessed national drinking-water infrastructure need

observations.method: EPA's 7th Drinking Water Infrastructure Needs Survey and Assessment and 2025 service-line update; projections and reported inventories are kept separate from completed replacement and household exposure.
observations.uncertainty: The service-line counts include projections and unknown-material inference, while the needs assessment is a long-term infrastructure estimate. These measures do not reveal which households received replacement, interim protection, notice, or safer water.
observations.subgroup: Public water systems, service lines, states, and communities; household and building-level incidence is not supplied in the national summary.
observations.counterinterpretation: Inventory and funding can improve identification and replacement without immediately changing household exposure; large assessed need is not a measure of annual failure or realized harm.

observations.period: July 2026; public-water versus private-well coverage and contamination responsibility

denominator.unit: U.S. population; published national coverage shares

community_water_system.unit: percent of people getting drinking water from a community water system

private_well.unit: approximately percent of Americans getting drinking water from a private well

sampled_private_wells_with_chemical_cont.unit: approximately percent of sampled private wells with at least one chemical at a potentially health-affecting level

federal_private_well_regulation.value: not generally regulated at the federal level

observations.method: CDC Environmental Health Tracking summary using public-water and private-well indicators; the well contamination estimate applies to sampled wells, not all private wells.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not identify each household's exposure, treatment, testing frequency, income, remediation, or health outcome. Sampled wells may not represent all private wells.
observations.subgroup: Residents using community water systems versus private wells; private-well oversight and responsibility vary by state and household.
observations.counterinterpretation: Private-well ownership can offer local control and may be safe when tested and maintained; contamination in sampled wells does not establish illness or universal private-well risk.

related_sources.claim: EPA's FY2026 milestones describe replacement funding, implementation resources, and public engagement work.
GAO documents financial and access challenges in water-infrastructure resilience assistance.

boundary: This record establishes national infrastructure need, service-line inventory/projection, public-versus-private water governance, and sampled-well contamination indicators. It does not establish a household's water exposure, replacement receipt, bill, repair, health outcome, local acceptance, or durable service security.
